findings.highlight: "I got my license during university… though it's only a certification."
findings.evidenceJa:
「免許なら大学の時取りましたけど…
でも、ペーパーですよ？」
findings.explanation: ペーパードライバー means Haruki has a license but no real driving practice; 'it's only a certification' is not idiomatic English and does not convey that fact.
findings.japanese:
「免許なら大学の時取りましたけど…
でも、ペーパーですよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I got my license during university… though it's only a certification."

findings.highlight: "Well, things like that happen, and I actually owed one of their guys a favor."
findings.evidenceJa:
「まぁそのこともあって、
向こうさんにも恩返しの必要があってな」
findings.explanation: Hamada says their editorial side owes Ensemble a favor for yielding the scoop; the English makes it Hamada's personal debt to an unspecified individual.
findings.japanese:
「まぁそのこともあって、
向こうさんにも恩返しの必要があってな」
findings.todokanai: "Well, things like that happen, and I actually owed one of their guys a favor."

findings.highlight: I uncomfortably wonder whether my blunt rejection didn't come across as all too unnatural
findings.evidenceJa: そんないやらしい計算をしながら
findings.explanation: Haruki deliberately calculates whether the others noticed how obstinately and unnaturally he refused the Touma assignment. The translation retains discomfort and suspicion but deletes his admission that he is making a self-serving calculation.
findings.japanese:
実は頑なに拒絶していたことを、
不自然に思われなかったかなって…
そんないやらしい計算をしながら。
findings.todokanai: And I uncomfortably wonder whether my blunt rejection didn't come across as all too unnatural.

findings.highlight: has been unsuitable for living in for over three years
findings.evidenceJa: 三年ほど前から、人の住む場所じゃなくなっていた
findings.explanation: The old Touma residence has ceased to be anyone's home and has stood unoccupied for about three years. The translation asserts that the building became physically unsuitable for habitation.
findings.japanese:
やっと辿り着いた場所は…
もう三年ほど前から、人の住む場所じゃなくなっていた。
findings.todokanai: And the place I reach… is a place that has been unsuitable for living in for over three years.

findings.highlight: I don't get it at all
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls herself truly unlucky for fleeing one unwanted meeting only to encounter Haruki at the ruined house. The translation changes bad luck into incomprehension.
findings.japanese:
「そしたら、こんな…
本当、ついてない」
findings.todokanai: "And yet, when I came here… I don't get it at all."

findings.highlight: the memories left by the three of us are long gone
findings.evidenceJa: 三人の思い出を残すものはもう跡形もなくなってて
findings.explanation: What has vanished are the physical traces and objects that preserve the three friends' memories, not the memories themselves; both characters are vividly remembering them in this scene.
findings.japanese:
けれどそこに、三人の思い出を残すものは
もう跡形もなくなってて…
findings.todokanai: But the memories left by the three of us are long gone, without any trace being left behind…

findings.highlight: "There are Japanese artists working harder than me overseas, yet no one even bats an eye at them…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「向こうであたしより活躍してる
日本人のアーティストなんてごまんといる。
なのに、その人たちには目も向けないで…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says many Japanese artists are more active or successful than she is overseas; 'working harder than me' changes professional achievement into moralized effort.
findings.japanese:
「向こうであたしより活躍してる
日本人のアーティストなんてごまんといる。
なのに、その人たちには目も向けないで…」
findings.todokanai: "There are Japanese artists working harder than me overseas, yet no one even bats an eye at them…"

findings.highlight: She did take offense in the end
findings.evidenceJa: 結局、買ってしまったけど
findings.explanation: Continuing the stock pairing of selling and buying words, Haruki says he ultimately took Kazusa's bait and answered her provocation. The translation assigns the reaction to Kazusa instead.
findings.todokanai: …She did take offense in the end.

findings.highlight: What an awful celebrity you are. Or perhaps that kind of attitude is par for the course in the celebrity world?
findings.evidenceJa: 最低の芸人だな。あ、それとも芸術家ならそういうのＯＫなんだっけ
findings.explanation: Haruki needles Kazusa by contrasting geinin, an entertainer, with geijutsuka, an artist: perhaps ignoring fans is unacceptable for the former but permitted for the latter. The translation calls both roles celebrities and erases the distinction driving the jab.
findings.japanese:
「ファンの声は無視かよ…最低の芸人だな。
あ、それとも芸術家ならそういうのＯＫなんだっけ？」
findings.todokanai: "You're going to ignore the voices of your fans? What an awful celebrity you are. Or perhaps that kind of attitude is par for the course in the celebrity world?"

findings.explanation: Kazusa makes only a choked, nonverbal reaction after Haruki's apology. The translation invents an explicit judgment that he has not changed.

findings.evidenceJa: 結論が出てないのかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki says they may not yet have reached a conclusion about whether these concerns are truly unnecessary. The translation adds permanent unknowability.
findings.japanese:
…余計なことなのかどうかは
結論が出てないのかもしれないけど。
findings.todokanai: …Though whether those things truly are unnecessary or not, we may never find out.

findings.highlight: I haven't met any of my friends from work since New Year's yet
findings.evidenceJa: 年明けてまだ誰も友達に会えてない
findings.explanation: Setsuna says work has been so busy since New Year that she has not seen any of her friends. The translation invents that the friends are coworkers.
findings.japanese:
「仕事は順調。
…順調すぎて、年明けてまだ誰も友達に会えてない」
findings.todokanai: "Work is going well… Too well, because I haven't met any of my friends from work since New Year's yet."

findings.highlight: the work bag laid on my bed
findings.evidenceJa: 床の上に置かれた通勤鞄
findings.explanation: Haruki looks at the work bag placed on the floor, specifically at the magazine inside it. The translation relocates the bag to his bed.
findings.japanese:
俺の視線が、床の上に置かれた通勤鞄に向けられる。
正確には、その中に収められた…
findings.todokanai: My eyes dart toward the work bag laid on my bed. Specifically, my eyes dart toward the contents of the bag…

findings.highlight: I would still have been able to make a cowardly excuse to get out of trouble, such as "I wasn't allowed to tell you."
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にはまだ、卑怯者から逃れるチャンスはあった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even after failing to tell Setsuna before the interview, he still had later opportunities to escape being a coward by confessing. The translation turns that moral opportunity into an opportunity to remain cowardly by fabricating an excuse.
findings.japanese:
それに、あの時話せなかったからと言って、
俺にはまだ、卑怯者から逃れるチャンスはあった。
findings.todokanai: Moreover, I would still have been able to make a cowardly excuse to get out of trouble, such as "I wasn't allowed to tell you."
